note: The most philosophically aligned prospect in the batch and the furthest outside the stated ICP. Not_deconditioned is a clear match — he trains three to five times a week, walks 10,000 to 20,000 steps a day, has previously had abs and done pull-ups, and is the opposite of gym-averse. Everything else fails. Successful: he had to leave his job because of his injuries and is now "in between jobs and self-employed", so the business-owner-or-physician test is not met on any current evidence. Income: $6,000 is "like six months of my rent", he declined to discuss his finances at all, and the financing quote left him "overwhelmed". Neglected_health: health is not the neglected corner of an otherwise good life, it is the thing that has taken his job, his sport and his mobility — "because of the injuries, I found my life just becoming more and more inhibited." Good_to_great: explicitly a return, not an advance — "I would love to look like I used to two years ago, three years ago." Two observations for the rollup. First, this is the third call in this batch where the decisive disqualifier is clinical and the stated ICP has no clinical criterion to catch it — an unresolved shoulder under investigation and a wrist already injured by kettlebells read as nothing at all against these five tests. Second, ICP fit and buying enthusiasm are inversely related across this batch: the prospect who most believes in the method, has watched the content for years, has spousal endorsement and answered the commitment question without hesitation is also the one who matches one criterion out of five.
